title: The Fewest Arrows That Burst Every Balloon

concept.title: Shoot at the right end of the balloon that ends first: it bursts everything that starts before that point
body: Balloons float on a line; the balloon `i` covers all the points from `a[i]` to `b[i]` (both ends included). An arrow shot at the point `x` bursts **every balloon that covers `x`**. What is the **smallest number of arrows** that burst all balloons? For the balloons `1-6, 2-8, 7-12, 10-16` the answer is 2: one arrow at 6 bursts the first two, one at 12 bursts the last two.

This is the *stabbing* problem for intervals. Sort the balloons by the **right end**. The first balloon has to be burst by some arrow, and the best place for it is its **right end** `b`: any arrow that bursts this balloon is at most `b`, and moving it to `b` can only help, because every balloon that starts at or before `b` and ends at or after the old position still covers `b` (the balloons are sorted by their right end, so none of the remaining ends before `b`).

body.code:
balloons.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])      # by the right end
arrows = 0
shot = -1                              # the position of the last arrow
for a, b in balloons:
    if a > shot:                       # this balloon was missed by the last arrow
        arrows += 1
        shot = b                       # shoot at its right end
print(arrows)

body: Balloons that touch at a single point (like `1-5` and `5-9`) share the point 5, so one arrow bursts both. The algorithm is the same as the one for choosing the most non-overlapping meetings: the number of arrows equals the largest set of balloons no two of which share a point. Time O(n log n).

statement: `n` balloons are given as ranges `[a, b]` of a line (the ends belong to the balloon). An arrow shot at a point bursts every balloon that contains the point. Print the smallest number of arrows that burst all balloons.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of balloons.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `a` and `b`: the balloon covers every point from `a` to `b` on the line.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of arrows.

examples.note: An arrow at 6 and an arrow at 12: 2.
The arrows at 5 and 13 (or at 5 and 9): the neighbours touch: 2.

hints: Shoot at the right end of the first balloon that was not burst yet.
A balloon is burst by the last arrow if its left end is not after the arrow position.

explanation: The balloons are sorted by their right end; whenever a balloon starts after the position of the last arrow, a new arrow is shot at its right end.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
balloons = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

balloons.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
arrows = 0
shot = -1
for a, b in balloons:
    if a > shot:
        arrows += 1
        shot = b
print(arrows)
